slot.brief: Find the chord of contact of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle, then use it to compute a length or prove a pole-polar property at level 4 difficulty.

stem: Tangents from $P=(16,-4)$ touch the circle $x^2+y^2-6x+8y=0$ at $A$ and $B$. Find the perimeter of triangle $PAB$.

verdicts.working: The circle has center �C=(3,-4)� and radius 5; �PC=13�. Hence �PA=PB=��\sqrt{13^2-5^2}=12�. The contact chord is at distance �25/13� from the center, so �AB=2\sqrt{5^2-(25/13)^2}=120/13�. Perimeter �=24+120/13=432/13�.

working:
Circle centre $(3,-4)$, radius $5$; $PC=13$, so $PA=PB=\sqrt{13^2-5^2}=12$. Chord of contact: $13(x-3)=25$, so $x=\dfrac{64}{13}$. Thus $AB=2\sqrt{25-\left(\dfrac{25}{13}\right)^2}=\dfrac{120}{13}$; perimeter $=24+\dfrac{120}{13}=\dfrac{432}{13}$.
